newsitem.title: MALI: Mali says its gold mines can weather price fall.
newsitem.headline: Mali says its gold mines can weather price fall.

text.p: Mali's energy minister said on Wednesday that low costs would allow gold mines there to withstand recent world gold price falls.

"With production costs of between $160 to $180 an ounce we still have sufficient margins to face current lower world prices which recently went down to $320 a ounce," energy minister Cheickna Seydi Diawara told Reuters.
New technologies had kept mine costs down in Mali, he added. Mines were also generally open cast which required less energy inputs than deeper mines elsewhere, he said.
South Africa's Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd is building up production at its Syama gold mine, one of Mali's largest, as well as exploring reserves at other sites.
"The new restructuring plan brought in this year by the company should allow production costs to be brought down to $160 an ounce from $304," Diawara said.
Mali's other large mine, Sadiola, which is owned by Australian group Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd, had one of the lowest production costs at $160 an ounce, he added.
Gold mining has expanded rapidly in Mali and other African countries since 1990 as governments have opened mining to foreign investment.

Regional gold-bearing geological structures underlying Sadiola could prove to be of world importance, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd business development manager Alan McKerron said recently, adding that Sadiola's estimated geological reserve was 140 tonnes.
